prompt: Roadmap III, Prompt 208, telescopes and resolution over the existing PSF (tranche T3 by D-R10-207-01)
committed: before the kernel module, the validator, the oracle script, its results, the telescope field, the instrument, the investigation and the tests of Prompt 208 existed; the constants quoted below were computed by scipy 1.13.1 (scipy.special, scipy.optimize.brentq) outside the repository
rule: A crossed bound is a failed check, recorded in failed-legs.json and left failing; only Carl resets one. A leg that cannot be measured is NOT RUN and says why. Nothing here was tuned against the kernel: the kernel did not exist when this file was written.

scope.built: an Airy point-spread function for a circular aperture with an optional central obstruction; a Moffat seeing profile; their convolution; light-gathering power; plate scale; the Rayleigh separation and the pair dip; a synthetic double star and faint field rendered through the detector kernel's frame model and measured with Prompt 183's PSF tool; one panel; one investigation at three depths
scope.notBuilt: adaptive optics, a Kolmogorov phase screen, wavelength-dependent seeing, atmospheric dispersion, aberrations, a spider, a hexagonal or segmented aperture, a detector MTF, a pixel-response function other than the box, polychromatic bands (one wavelength), real facilities (Prompt 209), authentic frames (A1)

constants.source: scipy.special.jn_zeros(1, 3); the root of 2 J1(x)/x = 1/sqrt(2) by brentq (x = 1.6163399483107015, FWHM = 2 x / pi lambda/D); 1 - J0(z)^2 - J1(z)^2 at each zero; twice the Airy intensity at half the first zero; Born and Wolf, Principles of Optics, 7th ed., section 8.5.2 and Table 8.2 (83.8, 91.0 and 93.8 percent inside the first three dark rings; the Rayleigh pair midpoint at 73.5 percent of the peak)

checks.bound: an unobstructed Airy pattern's first three dark rings lie where J1(x) = 0, x = pi D theta / lambda: the kernel's first dark-ring angle (the Rayleigh angle) equals 3.8317059702 lambda / (pi D), the second and third equal their zeros, each to a relative 1e-8, and the intensity at each is at most 1e-12 of the peak
the unobstructed Airy FWHM is 1.028993969962187 lambda / D to a relative 1e-8, and the kernel's intensity at half that angle is one half of the peak to an absolute 1e-10

the unobstructed encircled energy 1 - J0(x)^2 - J1(x)^2 at the first three dark rings is 0.8377848692, 0.9099305351 and 0.9376474743 to an absolute 1e-9 (Born and Wolf's table to three digits agrees: 0.838, 0.910, 0.938); it is 0 at the centre and rises monotonically on 400 points to 40 lambda / D; the kernel's numerical encircled energy for an obstructed aperture reduces to the closed form at obstruction 0 to an absolute 1e-9

for obstructions 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.5 the intensity [2 J1(x)/x - e^2 2 J1(e x)/(e x)]^2 / (1 - e^2)^2 against scipy at 400 radii to an absolute 1e-9 of the peak, the peak is 1, the first dark ring is the first root of J1(x) - e J1(e x) (brentq) to a relative 1e-8, and the encircled energy inside that ring against scipy quad of the intensity to an absolute 1e-8

for beta 1.5, 2.5, 4.765 and 10 the Moffat profile (beta - 1)/(pi alpha^2) (1 + r^2/alpha^2)^-beta integrates to 1 (scipy quad of 2 pi r I(r) to infinity) to a relative 1e-9, its FWHM is 2 alpha sqrt(2^(1/beta) - 1) to a relative 1e-12, and the closed-form encircled energy 1 - (1 + r^2/alpha^2)^(1 - beta) matches the quadrature at five radii to an absolute 1e-10

two equal unobstructed Airy patterns separated by the Rayleigh angle sum to a midpoint intensity of 0.735031662423 of the peak (a 26.5 percent dip) to an absolute 1e-9; the pair is not a dip (midpoint above 0.99) at 0.3 of the Rayleigh angle and a clear dip (below 0.5) at 1.6

the Rayleigh angle and the FWHM are different quantities even for a pure Airy pattern: their ratio is 1.185303244597 (3.8317059702 / (2 x 1.6163399483)) to a relative 1e-8, and the kernel exposes the two under different names

light-gathering power is the ratio of collecting areas D^2 (1 - e^2): 0.4 m with obstruction 0.3 against 0.1 m with none is 14.56, and against the dark-adapted eye (7 mm pupil) is 0.1456 / 0.000049 = 2971.428571428571 to a relative 1e-12; the plate scale is 206264.80624709636 arcsec per radian over the focal length: a 3.2 m focal length and a 10 micron pixel is 0.644577519522 arcsec, to a relative 1e-12; the focal length is the focal ratio times the aperture

the combined profile (the Moffat seeing convolved with the Airy pattern, by the product of their transfer functions) tends to its two limits: with a seeing FWHM of 1e-3 of the Airy FWHM it equals the Airy profile to an absolute 2e-4 of the peak at 200 radii out to 8 lambda / D, and with an Airy FWHM of 1e-3 of the seeing FWHM it equals the Moffat profile to an absolute 2e-4 of the peak at 200 radii out to 3 seeing FWHM; its encircled energy is 0 at 0 and increases monotonically

an independent numerical diffraction calculation (numpy FFT of a sampled, anti-aliased annular pupil, Fraunhofer diffraction, azimuthally averaged; no Bessel function and no Gravitas code) at two apertures, A: D = 0.25 m, obstruction 0, 550 nm and B: D = 1.0 m, obstruction 0.30, 700 nm, pinned as a fixture: the kernel's Airy profile equals the pinned profile to an absolute 5e-4 of the peak at every pinned radius out to 8 lambda / D, and its encircled energy at 1, 2, 3 and 5 lambda / D to an absolute 1e-3

the same two apertures with a Moffat seeing profile of FWHM 1.2 arcsec (A) and 0.6 arcsec (B) and beta 4.765, the oracle forming the combined profile by two-dimensional FFT convolution of the pupil PSF with the sampled Moffat: the kernel's combined profile (a different algorithm: the product of transfer functions and an inverse Hankel transform) equals the pinned profile to an absolute 2e-3 of the peak at every pinned radius out to 3 combined FWHM, its FWHM to a relative 2e-3 and its encircled energy at 1, 2 and 3 FWHM to an absolute 3e-3

the frame model's point-spread function through a supplied profile conserves light: the electrons a noiseless rendered star puts on the frame equal its rate times the exposure times the profile's encircled energy at the rendering reach, to a relative 2e-3 at pixel scales of 0.15, 0.5 and 1.5 times the Airy FWHM, and the model's own default (no profile supplied) is bit-identical to the version before this prompt on a fixed seeded frame

ensemble coverage through Prompt 183's PSF tool: 200 seeded frames of one star, telescope D = 0.25 m, obstruction 0.30, focal ratio 8, a 10 micron pixel (1.031 arcsec per pixel), 550 nm, seeing 2.0 arcsec (Moffat, beta 4.765), V = 15.5, exposure 60 s, a 64 by 64 frame, a sky of V = 20 per square arcsec; detection at 4 sigma, the Moffat model fitted to the brightest source: the fraction of frames whose stated 1 sigma interval on the FWHM contains the FWHM of the kernel's combined profile is within the 1 sigma binomial-plus-margin band, and the mean relative bias is small

a diffraction-limited frame is not a Moffat: 50 seeded frames of one star at D = 0.25 m, obstruction 0.30, focal ratio 50 (0.165 arcsec per pixel), 550 nm, seeing 0, V = 13, exposure 30 s, 64 by 64: the tool must flag the model as limiting (its reduced chi-square above its own threshold) in at least 90 percent of them; the panel's own number is then labelled a model fit, not the pattern's width

every one of these is refused with a coded error and no number: an obstruction of 1 or more (it is the aperture's own diameter or larger) or below 0, NaN, a string; an aperture, wavelength, focal length or pixel of 0, a negative number, NaN or Infinity; a Moffat beta of 1 or less; a negative seeing FWHM; an exposure of 0 or less for a frame; the kernel never returns NaN for an accepted input over a seeded domain of 500 draws (aperture 0.02 to 10 m, obstruction 0 to 0.9, wavelength 300 to 2500 nm, seeing 0 to 5 arcsec, beta 1.5 to 10)

limits.domain: aperture 0.02-10 m, obstruction 0-0.9, wavelength 300-2500 nm, seeing 0-5 arcsec, beta 1.5-10

claimRule.intent: The FWHM is a measured width of a profile; the Rayleigh separation is a criterion for a diffraction pattern. No lesson text calls the FWHM the resolution limit or says the Rayleigh separation is what a frame measured, and no lesson text says magnification is what a telescope is for.

badControls: The FWHM is the resolution limit of the telescope.
The resolution limit is simply the measured FWHM.
Magnification is what a telescope is for.
A telescope's main job is to magnify.
The Rayleigh separation was measured from the frame.
El FWHM es el límite de resolución del telescopio.
El límite de resolución es la anchura a media altura medida.
El aumento es lo que importa en un telescopio.
permittedControls: The FWHM is the measured width of the star's profile; the Rayleigh separation is a criterion for two diffraction patterns.
Magnification makes the image larger; it adds no detail the aperture and the seeing did not already allow.
The Rayleigh separation and the measured FWHM are different quantities and they differ even with no atmosphere.
El FWHM es la anchura medida del perfil de la estrella; la separación de Rayleigh es un criterio para dos patrones de difracción.
La ampliación agranda la imagen; no añade detalle que la apertura y el seeing no permitieran ya.
